reasons: Deviation classification is correct: Section 13.1 grants the Services licence to 'Customer alone', expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no mechanism to add them, and makes the licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — this fails the fallback (affiliates covered at least on written notice) and sits in the rule's walk-away territory, so the other grant clauses (13.2 limited to paid-up software/Vendor Technology; 13.3 covering transfer and revocation standard) do not cure the Services grant.

Redline is valid and actionable: it inserts 'its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf', removes the at-will revocation by cross-referencing the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in Section 13.3, and deletes the now-contradictory 'without Affiliates or contractors' carve-out; the resulting sentence is grammatical and self-consistent.

Edit is appropriately restrained: 'non-transferable' is left intact because successor/Affiliate transfer is already handled in 13.3, so no duplicative change is proposed. The failed minimal-edit check (0.776 changed-character ratio) is an artifact of a very short clause whose exclusionary language had to be removed to reach the playbook position.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, cites the playbook position and the internal cross-reference, and does not overstate the change.
